stemMd: A cone and cylinder have the same base radius and height. How does the cone’s volume compare with the cylinder’s?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It is three times as large.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is one ninth as large.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is one third as large.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It is one half as large.

explanationMd: Cylinder volume is πr²h, whereas cone volume is πr²h/3. With identical r and h, their ratio is exactly one third. No extra length scaling is involved.

distractorRationale.e: The cone volume formula has factor one third, not one half.
distractorRationale.d: Equal base and height do not make these different solids have equal volumes.
distractorRationale.b: This squares a factor that is already a volume ratio.
